name_en: Tamago kanten — a sweet-salty egg-and-soy jelly for festival days
summary_ja: 溶かした寒天に溶き卵、醤油、砂糖を加えて冷やし固める庄内のお菓子で、祭りや正月に作られる甘じょっぱい一品という。日常的な食材の寒天と当時貴重だった卵が結びつき、行事食として親しまれてきたと伝わる。
summary_en: Melted kanten is mixed with beaten egg, soy sauce, and sugar, then chilled until set — a Shonai sweet made for festivals and New Year, sweet and salty at once. It is said to have grown out of pairing everyday kanten with egg, once a precious ingredient, into a dish for special occasions.
source_title: 卵寒天　/　醤油寒天 山形県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Kujira mochi — a steamed rice-flour cake with walnuts, named for its old bulk
summary_ja: 米粉に砂糖とくるみを混ぜて蒸し上げる餅菓子で、くじらの肉は使わないが、昔は今より大きく作られその大きさをくじらに例えたなど諸説あるという。旧暦の桃の節句に雛壇へ供える新庄発祥の菓子と伝わる。
summary_en: Rice flour, sugar, and walnuts steamed together into a mochi cake that contains no whale at all — its name is said to come from the loaves once being made whale-sized, among other theories. It is said to have originated in Shinjo and is offered at the old-calendar Doll's Festival.
source_title: くじら餅 山形県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Sasamaki — glutinous rice bundled in bamboo grass and boiled for Boys' Day
summary_ja: 水切りしたもち米を笹の葉で巻いて結び、熱湯で茹で上げたものにきなこと砂糖をかけて食べる端午の節句の行事食。鶴岡市南部には灰汁水で煮て黄色くぷるんとした食感に仕上げる珍しい作り方も残るという。
summary_en: Drained glutinous rice is wrapped and tied in bamboo grass leaves, boiled, and eaten dusted with sweetened soybean flour — a food for the Boys' Day festival. In the southern part of Tsuruoka, an unusual method boils it in lye water instead, turning the rice yellow and springy.
source_title: 笹巻き 山形県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
